slice_results.behavior_summary: When called, the code modifies the DOM by creating a canvas element, drawing a rotated watermark text using configuration from window.pageConfig, then overlays a fixed-position div with the canvas image as a repeating background. It accesses and modifies DOM elements and styles but does not perform any network, file, or system operations, nor does it handle suspicious data such as hardcoded IPs, URLs, or shell commands, resulting in a purely visual watermarking behavior without security impact.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code creates a visual watermark overlay by drawing text on a canvas and applying it as a repeating background on a fixed-position div. It only manipulates DOM elements and styles without any network requests, obfuscation, or attempts to capture sensitive user input. Compared to the known malicious patterns, it does not inject scripts from external domains, does not solicit sensitive user actions, nor does it perform any suspicious data exfiltration or system manipulation. The behavior is consistent with a benign UI enhancement for watermarking purposes.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime, the code creates and injects a DOM overlay element into the webpage, presenting a prompt for the user to connect their crypto wallet or scan a QR code. This overlay captures user interaction and can redirect sensitive wallet credentials or session data to attacker-controlled infrastructure, resulting in potential credential theft or wallet compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The injection of a UI overlay that solicits sensitive actions, such as connecting a crypto wallet or scanning a QR code, is a hallmark of phishing attacks. This behavior is highly anomalous for an animation rendering library and is designed to deceive users into divulging credentials or authorizing malicious transactions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate @lottiefiles/lottie-player package should only provide animation rendering capabilities and never prompt users for wallet connections, display overlays unrelated to animation, or interact with cryptocurrency features.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate wallet connection prompts are only expected in cryptocurrency wallet extensions or decentralized applications (dApps), not in generic animation libraries like lottie-player. Any such prompt in this context is highly suspicious.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automated scanners should analyze JavaScript bundles for hardcoded domain allow-lists combined with destructive DOM actions, such as setting document.body.innerHTML to an empty string. Flag any package or code that erases the UI based on environment variables or production checks. Review for the presence of sabotage logic that disables the application outside of specific domains, especially when tied to environment variables like VUE_APP_SECRET_KEY and NODE_ENV.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At runtime in the browser, the injected code appends a script tag with src set to https://send.wagateway.pro/client.js?cache=ignore to the DOM, causing the browser to fetch and execute additional malicious JavaScript from the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and mass-injected into all JavaScript files, ensuring that every page load triggers the download and execution of untrusted code from an external domain controlled by the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not inject remote scripts from unrelated or untrusted domains into all JavaScript files, especially using obfuscation and without user or developer consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script loading is sometimes used for analytics or feature toggles, but not in an obfuscated, repository-wide, and externally controlled manner.
key_indicators: Obfuscated JavaScript injected into all *.js files
Dynamically creates a script tag with src pointing to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
No legitimate business logic—sole purpose is to load further code from an attacker-controlled domain
Script tag uses a unique id (hook-loader) to avoid duplicate injection

execution_context.trigger: At runtime in the browser when any modified JavaScript file is loaded
execution_context.file_location: assets/js/*.js (appended to the end of every JavaScript file in the repository)

The entire commit is malicious, targeting both developer and user security by stealing secrets and injecting credential-stealing code.

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains a developer's GitHub personal access token (PAT), likely via a separate malicious package or phishing.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to authenticate as the victim and push code to their repositories.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the stolen PAT to commit malicious code to the victim's repositories, impersonating Dependabot to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is introduced into the repository under the guise of a trusted automation tool.

attack_chain.action: A malicious GitHub Actions workflow is added to exfiltrate repository secrets and variables on every push event.
attack_chain.leads_to: Repository secrets and variables are sent to the attacker's command and control (C2) server.

attack_chain.action: All JavaScript files in the repository are modified to append an obfuscated script loader that fetches additional malicious code from an external domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-users of the web application are exposed to further malicious payloads when they load the compromised JavaScript files.

attack_chain.action: The loaded remote script intercepts password form submissions in the browser and exfiltrates credentials to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: End-user credentials are stolen and sent to the attacker's C2 server, achieving the attacker's final objective.

behavioral_signatures: Addition or modification of GitHub Actions workflows that POST repository secrets or variables to external domains
Mass modification of JavaScript (*.js) files to append obfuscated script loaders
JavaScript code that dynamically injects script tags with src pointing to suspicious external domains
Client-side code that intercepts password form submissions and sends serialized form data to untrusted endpoints
file_indicators: .github/workflows/hook.yml (new or modified workflow file)
Obfuscated JavaScript code appended to the end of assets/js/*.js files
Presence of script tags with id 'hook-loader' and src set to send.wagateway.pro/client.js
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new or modified GitHub Actions workflows that serialize and POST secrets or variables to external domains. Scan for mass changes to JavaScript files, especially for obfuscated code that injects remote scripts from send.wagateway.pro. Detect client-side code that attaches event listeners to password forms and exfiltrates credentials. Flag any network traffic to send.wagateway.pro domains as a high-confidence indicator of compromise.

matched_snippet.code_behavior: At import-time, the code dynamically creates a <script> element, sets its source to a remote attacker-controlled domain (castleservices01.com), injects it into the DOM, and loads additional malicious JavaScript, resulting in the execution of a crypto drainer payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code injects a remote script from an untrusted, unrelated domain at import-time, which is a classic supply chain attack technique for delivering further malicious payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate animation library should not load or execute external scripts from domains outside its official infrastructure, especially not from suspicious or unrelated domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some analytics or feature flag services may load remote scripts, but only from trusted, well-known domains with transparent purposes.
key_indicators: Dynamic creation and injection of <script> elements
References to castleservices01.com or other non-LottieFiles domains
Script loading at import-time rather than user action
Obfuscated or non-obvious code inclusion in main bundle

package_info.why_malicious: Versions 2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7 of the lottie-player npm package were compromised in a supply chain attack. The attacker injected code that loads a remote crypto drainer script, which prompts users to connect their cryptocurrency wallets and then exfiltrates assets (cryptocurrency and NFTs) to attacker-controlled addresses. This malicious behavior is unrelated to the legitimate functionality of an animation library and poses a severe risk to users.

attack_chain.action: Malicious lottie-player package is loaded by the website (via CDN or npm), triggering the import-time execution of injected code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Loads remote drainer script from attacker-controlled domain (castleservices01.com).

attack_chain.action: The drainer script, once loaded, injects a wallet connect UI and prompts the user to connect their crypto wallet.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is deceived into connecting their wallet, granting access to wallet information.

attack_chain.action: Upon wallet connection, the script exfiltrates wallet information and initiates unauthorized transactions to steal assets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's cryptocurrency and NFTs are transferred to attacker-controlled addresses.

behavioral_signatures: Dynamic script injection from domains not affiliated with LottieFiles (e.g., castleservices01.com) during import-time of lottie-player.js
Wallet connect prompts or web3 wallet access requests on sites not expected to interact with cryptocurrency wallets
Outbound WebSocket or HTTP(S) connections to known phishing or drainer domains (e.g., castleservices01.com) following wallet connection
file_indicators: dist/lottie-player.js containing references to castleservices01.com or similar suspicious domains
Presence of dynamically injected <script> elements with src attributes pointing to external drainer payloads
Unexpected modifications or additions to lottie-player.js in npm package versions 2.0.5, 2.0.6, or 2.0.7
network_indicators: Any network connections (HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket) to castleservices01.com
Outbound requests to domains with a history of crypto phishing or drainer activity after loading animation libraries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for external script loads initiated by lottie-player.js, especially from domains not associated with LottieFiles. Flag any wallet connect prompts or web3 wallet access requests on sites that do not provide crypto-related functionality. Detect and alert on outbound network connections to known drainer or phishing domains (such as castleservices01.com) after loading animation libraries. Use file integrity monitoring to detect unauthorized changes or suspicious references in npm package files, particularly in dist/lottie-player.js for the affected versions.
